reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds on record.

The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and each refund is smaller than its order, so I see no concrete problem. I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme, rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance of 54385 matches my own check (orders 200 and 203 total 73072, less refund 203 of 18687). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 40147 matches my own check (orders 201 and 204 total 44020, less refund 201 of 3873). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 33079 matches my check (orders 202 and 205 total 33079, with no refunds on record). Alpha's refunds are consistent with the ledger and the orders, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme at 54385.
Acme's payout of 54385 was recorded successfully. Next I'll record birch's payout using the verified net balance of 40147.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's net balance of 33079 matches my check (orders 202 and 205, no refunds). I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three customers have been paid, and each payout matched the net balance I verified against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the report.
